purpose: Demo case 1: every HGNS criterion met through the PAP intolerance pathway, so the copilot should mark it approve-ready quickly and cite each line.

patient.summary: 68-year-old man with moderate-to-severe obstructive sleep apnea, treated hypertension and high cholesterol; stopped CPAP after three months because of mask discomfort and air leak.

request.service_details: First implant of a complete hypoglossal nerve stimulator system for obstructive sleep apnea.

documents.title: Attended in-lab diagnostic polysomnogram
documents.guidance: Full PSG report: sleep architecture, total sleep time 7.2 hours, event table with counts and indices, oxygen nadir, 4% hypopnea rule named in the methods, interpretation of moderate-to-severe OSA.

documents.title: CPAP device compliance download
documents.guidance: 30-day download 2026-05-10 to 2026-06-08: average use, days used, percent of nights with 4 or more hours, large leak time, device-estimated AHI.

documents.title: Sleep medicine follow-up visit
documents.guidance: In-person visit with vitals. History of CPAP start, mask discomfort and air leak, nasal-pillow refit, stopping CPAP in June. Reviews the PSG and the DISE. No narcolepsy symptoms. Plan recommends HGNS and refers to ENT for implant.

documents.title: Drug-induced sleep endoscopy report
documents.guidance: VOTE-style description of velum, oropharynx, tongue base and epiglottis. Velum: complete anteroposterior collapse; explicitly no complete concentric collapse at the soft palate. Tonsils grade 1.

documents.title: ENT surgical consultation for HGNS
documents.guidance: Pre-surgical H&P with vitals and BMI, full past medical history (hypertension, high cholesterol, knee arthroscopy 2009), medications, no implanted devices, no neuromuscular disease, normal tongue movement, airway exam, assessment that he is a candidate and plan to schedule implant.

findings.rationale: 68 on the request date.
BMI 31.2 on 2026-09-20 is inside the 6-month window and below 35.0.
Most recent diagnostic study qualifies on every part.
In-lab PSG 7 months before the request date.
AHI 38.0 on the 4% rule is at least 15.
AHI 38.0 is no more than 65.
Central plus mixed share is 2.9%.
Recent DISE without complete concentric collapse.
DISE about 4 months before the request date.
Report states the soft-palate pattern and that it was not complete concentric.
In-person sleep visit with a recommendation.
In-person visit 7 weeks before the request date.
Explicit recommendation of HGNS.
Met through the intolerance pathway; the failure pathway is not used.
Every part of 7.15 is documented.
CPAP started 2026-04-10.
Clinician documents he stopped CPAP.
Mask discomfort and air leak named.
Mask refit dated before he stopped.
Device report shows low use.
22% of nights with 4+ hours is less than 70%.
Tonsils grade 1; listed to show a numeric contraindication checked and not triggered.

author_notes: Matches the kickoff demo script: BMI 31.2, AHI 38, sleep study 7 months old, CPAP intolerance, DISE result.
The device report's 22% and the consult's BMI 31.6 are the two places a careless extractor could pick the wrong value.
